authoritative_sources.title: Eczema
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CDA current disease-information page was checked directly at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: Recognize atopic dermatitis as the common hereditary eczema phenotype, typically with pruritic inflamed skin and an age- and site-pattern that commonly involves flexures, face, neck, or hands.

source_citations.locator: What is Eczema; Signs & Symptoms; Types of Eczema: Atopic dermatitis

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Eczema is a descriptive group of inflammatory dermatoses; a pruritic rash should not be labelled atopic dermatitis without considering contact and other eczematous causes.

source_citations.locator: What is Eczema; Types of Eczema

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports pattern recognition only and does not encode topical or systemic medication selection.

evidence_notes: Medication and escalation claims require later product- and patient-specific Canadian evidence.

authoritative_sources.title: Eczema
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CDA current disease-information page was checked directly at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: Differentiate eczematous dermatitis by exposure and morphology: allergic contact dermatitis follows delayed allergen exposure, while irritant contact dermatitis follows repeated chemically damaging exposure; dyshidrotic, nummular, seborrheic, stasis, and lichen simplex chronicus are additional eczema phenotypes.

source_citations.locator: Types of Eczema: Contact dermatitis and other types

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Patch testing is used to diagnose allergic contact dermatitis; it is not a test for all eczematous eruptions.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports morphology and exposure-based recognition, not treatment selection or occupational compensation decisions.

evidence_notes: Avoid converting a contact-dermatitis recognition packet into a medication regimen.

authoritative_sources.title: Practical guide for evaluation and management of beta-lactam allergy
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Society of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: This CSACI position statement remains a current Canadian structured-assessment source; its claims are limited to recognition and history-taking, not a universal treatment protocol.

supported_recommendations.statement: Assess a suspected drug eruption with a medication timeline and lesion morphology, explicitly checking for systemic symptoms, mucosal involvement, desquamation, and organ involvement that suggest a severe delayed reaction such as DRESS or SJS/TEN.

source_citations.locator: Clinical spectrum of beta-lactam hypersensitivity; history elements for suspected reactions

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: A remote or vague rash history does not by itself establish ongoing drug allergy; the Canadian assessment requires phenotype and exposure details.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports diagnostic characterization and safety triage; it does not specify rechallenge, testing, or treatment for a particular drug or rash.

evidence_notes: Future medication-specific claims require the applicable current Canadian monograph or specialty guidance.

authoritative_sources.title: Antifungal agents for common outpatient paediatric infections
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: CPS reaffirmed this national practice point in 2024.

supported_recommendations.statement: Recognize dermatophyte infection by site and morphology: tinea corporis presents as a superficial circular lesion on non-hair-bearing skin, while tinea pedis and onychomycosis involve feet and nails; microscopy or culture is useful when diagnosis is uncertain or nail disease requires organism differentiation.

source_citations.locator: Tinea corporis; Tinea pedis and onychomycosis

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: A clinically suspected nail fungus may be dermatophytic or non-dermatophytic; nail clippings for culture distinguish these possibilities.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports dermatophyte recognition and confirmation boundaries only; parasite, viral, yeast, and STI diagnoses require their own current evidence.

source_citations.locator: Scope; Tinea corporis; Tinea pedis and onychomycosis

evidence_notes: Do not infer pediatric dosing or adult treatment regimens from this diagnosis packet.

authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: PHAC identifies this as the current national guide hub and records its June 2026 updates.

authoritative_sources.title: Shingles (Herpes Zoster): Fact sheet
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The current PHAC page supports stable zoster pattern recognition only; it is not used for vaccination eligibility or antiviral treatment decisions.

supported_recommendations.statement: Recognize herpes zoster as reactivation of varicella-zoster virus causing a painful unilateral dermatomal blistering rash; for genital herpes or anogenital warts, use the current PHAC infection-specific STBBI guide for diagnostic and management claims.

source_citations.locator: What is shingles; How do people get shingles; What are the symptoms
STBBI guides: Genital herpes and Anogenital warts

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: This recognition packet does not establish antiviral selection or vaccine eligibility; those are current product- and program-specific decisions.

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: PHAC is the direct current Canadian national authority for STI guidance and shingles public-health information; these sources cover the required diagnosis boundary without an international fallback.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports lesion-pattern recognition and source selection, not treatment dosing, immunization schedules, or provincially funded-program eligibility.

source_citations.locator: Guide scope; updates to the guides

evidence_notes: Medication and immunization verifier flags require case-specific current Canadian sources at generation time.

authoritative_sources.title: Management of community-associated bacterial skin and soft tissue infections in children and prevention of recurrence
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: CPS current position statement was checked directly at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: Assess bacterial skin and soft-tissue infection by focused history, examination, and severity; obtain appropriate microbiology from purulent or open lesions, distinguish minor infection from rapidly progressive, deep, necrotizing, or systemically unwell presentations, and prioritize source-control assessment for abscesses.

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Superficial swabs have limited value; aspirated pus, drained-abscess material, or tissue is preferred when microbiology is required.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports syndrome recognition, severity, cultures, and source-control boundaries; it does not encode empiric regimen or duration.

evidence_notes: Any antibiotic selection must be derived later from current local antibiogram and patient-specific Canadian guidance.

authoritative_sources.title: Practical guide for evaluation and management of beta-lactam allergy
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Society of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: This CSACI position statement is used for the stable severe-reaction recognition boundary, not medication-specific management.

supported_recommendations.statement: A delayed drug eruption with fever, facial swelling or lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia, and possible hepatic, renal, hematologic, cardiac, pulmonary, or gastrointestinal involvement should raise concern for DRESS/DIHS and requires urgent assessment.

source_citations.locator: Clinical spectrum of beta-lactam hypersensitivity; severe type IV reaction history elements

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: A mild delayed rash without severe cutaneous or systemic features is not equivalent to DRESS.

source_citations.locator: History elements: mild delayed reaction versus severe cutaneous adverse drug reaction

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports severe-reaction recognition and urgent escalation, not a causative-drug list or corticosteroid protocol.

evidence_notes: Medication attribution and management require specialist and product-specific evidence.

authoritative_sources.title: Practical guide for evaluation and management of beta-lactam allergy
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Society of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: This CSACI position statement is used for delayed T-cell-mediated pustular eruption recognition only.

supported_recommendations.statement: In a new pustular eruption after medication exposure, recognize acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis as a severe delayed T-cell-mediated drug-hypersensitivity phenotype and distinguish it from non-drug pustular disorders through exposure history and urgent clinical assessment.

source_citations.locator: Clinical spectrum of beta-lactam hypersensitivity: Type IVd, pustular exanthema; severe reaction history

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Pustules alone do not establish AGEP; the temporal medication history and alternative infectious or inflammatory diagnoses remain material.

source_citations.locator: History elements for suspected drug reaction

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports recognition of a possible severe pustular drug reaction, not immunomodulator use or a drug-specific culprit list.

authoritative_sources.title: Practical guide for evaluation and management of beta-lactam allergy
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Society of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: This CSACI position statement is used for SJS/TEN recognition and exposure-history safety boundaries only.

supported_recommendations.statement: Mucosal lesions or ulcers, skin desquamation, blistering, or systemic symptoms after medication exposure are red flags for severe type IV reactions including SJS/TEN and require urgent assessment.

source_citations.locator: History elements: mucosal lesions, skin desquamation, and severe type IV reactions

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Not every drug-associated rash is SJS/TEN; mucosal, blistering, desquamative, and systemic features distinguish the emergency concern from mild delayed exanthems.

source_citations.locator: History elements: mild delayed reactions and severe cutaneous adverse drug reactions

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports emergency recognition and referral, not severity scoring, burn-unit criteria, or immunomodulatory treatment.

evidence_notes: SJS/TEN treatment claims need dedicated current emergency or specialty guidance.

source_citations.locator: History elements: severe type IV reactions

authoritative_sources.title: Update in Diagnosis and Management of Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions: Emerging Therapies and Evolving Presentations
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Current Canadian dermatology expert update; used only for recognition of generalized bullous fixed drug eruption within the severe cutaneous adverse-reaction differential.

supported_recommendations.statement: A suspected fixed drug eruption or photosensitivity reaction requires an exposure timeline and lesion morphology assessment; generalized bullous fixed drug eruption belongs in the severe cutaneous adverse-reaction differential and must be distinguished from SJS/TEN.

source_citations.locator: Abstract: severe cutaneous adverse reactions and generalized bullous fixed drug eruption; references to differential diagnosis

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Generalized bullous fixed drug eruption can mimic epidermal necrolysis; do not infer a benign fixed eruption when blistering or mucosal disease raises a severe-reaction concern.

source_citations.locator: Abstract and cited generalized bullous fixed drug eruption differential

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: This current Canadian dermatology expert publication directly addresses the severe fixed-drug-eruption differential; no current Canadian specialty-society guideline with equivalent scope was identified.

evidence_boundaries.statement: This packet supports recognition and differential boundaries only; it does not supply culprit-drug lists, phototesting protocols, or treatment recommendations.

source_citations.locator: Abstract: SCAR classification and differential diagnosis

evidence_notes: Photosensitivity-specific medication claims require later product-specific Canadian evidence.
